magi.detail: HealthCare.gov: MAGI "is adjusted gross income (AGI) plus these, if any: untaxed foreign income, non-taxable Social Security benefits, and tax-exempt interest." AGI is IRS Form 1040, line 11. The same MAGI concept is used for Medicaid and CHIP, and California's Medi-Cal MAGI rules implement 42 CFR 435.603.

The tax filer, the filer's spouse, and tax dependents — including people who do not need coverage. Medi-Cal household size rules have their own adjustments for children and tax dependents; see 42 CFR 435.603(d).

magi.value: Capital gains · investment income (interest, dividends) · rental and royalty income (net) · self-employment income · retirement/pension · Social Security (taxable and non-taxable) · tips · unemployment
magi.detail: This is HealthCare.gov's list of income types to count in a Marketplace application; the same MAGI methodology drives Medi-Cal income. Investment income includes "expected interest and dividends earned on investments, including tax-exempt interest." Rental income is counted net of expenses.

magi.item: Income types that do not count
magi.value: Gifts · child support · loan proceeds · SSI · workers' compensation · veterans' disability payments · child tax credit refunds
magi.detail: Also on the HealthCare.gov do-not-count list. Note that Supplemental Security Income is excluded from MAGI.

magi.value: The year of coverage, as a projection
magi.detail: "Marketplace savings are based on your expected household income for the year you want coverage, not last year's income." Make your best estimate — a wrong estimate can mean money back at tax time.

streams.value: Taxable rental amount, subject to deductions/loss limitations
streams.detail: IRS Publication 527 describes rental receipts, allowable expenses and loss limits. DHCS lists taxable Schedule E rental income. Gross rent and bank deposits are not automatically MAGI; the individual's figure has not been supplied.

streams.item: Property-management work (if it is a business)
streams.detail: If you are paid to manage property as a trade or business, HealthCare.gov lists self-employment income among the types to count: "Include the income you expect to make from your business after expenses. You'll also need to describe the type of work you do." Self-employment income is earned income, which would also change the work-requirement analysis.
Taxable interest enters MAGI, and tax-exempt interest may be added back under coverage MAGI rules. Account principal is not interest income; actual amount is unknown.

CFTC designation establishes the exchange's market status, not the federal tax character or gain/loss method for this person. General IRS investment rules do not supply a Kalshi-specific filing answer.
streams.flag: Tax character, deductible losses, reporting form and monthly countable amount are not established by the official material cited here; do not assert that trading gains automatically satisfy the $580 route.

streams.item: Does any of this count as "earned income" for the work rule?
streams.value: No — and the rule does not require earned income
streams.detail: The federal requirement is satisfied by 80 hours of work, community service, work-program participation or half-time school, or by an income test. California's statute frames the income test as "total monthly income, using modified adjusted gross income (MAGI)-based financial methods," and the member notice says "an income from any source." The $580 route does not require wages.

income-580.detail: $7.25 federal minimum wage × 80 hours. The federal minimum wage is $7.25 per hour, effective July 24, 2009, under the Fair Labor Standards Act. California requires states to use the federal minimum wage figure in this test — the state minimum wage is not used.

income-580.value: Total monthly income, MAGI-based financial methods
income-580.detail: WIC § 14005.69(e)(6): "The individual has a total monthly income, using modified adjusted gross income (MAGI)-based financial methods, as specified in Section 1396a(e)(14) of Title 42 of the United States Code, for their individual MAGI-based household budget, that is no less than the applicable minimum wage requirement … multiplied by 80 hours."

income-580.item: How DHCS's county guidance describes it
income-580.value: Earlier preliminary county letter uses "total gross income"
income-580.detail: ACWDL 25-30 includes a broad fluctuating-income example, but labels itself preliminary. The later federal CMS §435.552(f)–(g) and enacted California §14005.69(e)(6)–(7) specify MAGI-based household income and restrict six-month averaging to seasonal workers. Do not use the letter as a blanket permission to average trading gains.

income-580.item: How the member notice words it
income-580.value: "an income from any source of at least $580 (before taxes) in any month since your last renewal"
income-580.detail: The member notice describes income from any source before taxes and discusses variable hours/seasonal jobs. It is a plain-language notice, not a tax ruling on gross rental receipts, investment losses or event-contract payouts. Read alongside the later MAGI-based statute.

income-580.value: One month in the window, not every month
income-580.detail: At application: the calendar month immediately preceding your application month. At a six-month renewal: any one month since your last determination — months need not be consecutive. So one qualifying month in the window satisfies that renewal.

income-580.value: Average monthly income over the preceding 6 months of at least $580
income-580.detail: Applies to a seasonal worker as defined in section 45R(d)(5)(B) of the Internal Revenue Code. WIC § 14005.69(e)(7).

income-580.item: Reconciling earlier gross wording with operative MAGI-based methodology
income-580.detail: California §14005.69(e)(6) and CMS §435.552(f) specify MAGI-based household methods. The preliminary county letter and member notice use broader everyday language; neither establishes a tax-character shortcut for this person.
income-580.flag: The person's actual household MAGI, monthly timing, rental deductions and Kalshi tax character remain unknown. Seek a county determination if the evidence used for the monthly calculation is disputed.

examples.item: Earned wages not required for MAGI coverage
examples.detail: Eligibility must still be determined by the agency from actual household income, age and coverage facts; having no wages does not certify $0 MAGI.

examples.item: Actual countable rental result for this person
examples.detail: Taxable rental income can be affected by deductible expenses and passive-loss limitations.
examples.flag: Not provided. Gross deposits and hypothetical cash flow cannot establish taxable Schedule E income or monthly work-rule qualification.
